title: First Kashmir War
summary: In October 1947 tribal militias from Pakistan's North-West Frontier entered the princely state of Jammu and Kashmir. Maharaja Hari Singh asked India for help and signed an instrument of accession; Indian troops were flown to Srinagar and the fighting spread across the state. A UN-supervised ceasefire was in place by January 1949.

uncertainty.note: Opened sources give only October 1947 for the invasion. The Maharaja's letter is dated 26 October; a US telegram says the accession was signed 27 October while its footnote says 26 October, and Mountbatten accepted on 27 October. UN observers arrived 24 January 1949, while the National Army Museum says a UN-sponsored ceasefire ended the war in 1948.

importance.justification: It began the India-Pakistan dispute over Kashmir, which has driven later wars and remains unresolved.

related.because: Fighting broke out soon after independence and Partition, when Kashmir's ruler had not yet joined India or Pakistan.

beats.caption: Tribal militias from Pakistan entered Kashmir, and the Maharaja turned to India for help in exchange for accession.
Mountbatten accepted the accession and Indian troops were flown into Srinagar, where they repelled the invaders.
The first UN military observers arrived to supervise the India-Pakistan ceasefire in Jammu and Kashmir.
